A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OHRBench and contain readable main text, figures, tables, and supplementary material. The substantial revisions can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original OCR/RAG benchmark results, noise-sensitivity experiments, table-format comparisons, and VLM-input experiments, with additional results in the appendix.

after.justification: v2 reports original results on the revised benchmark, noise-sensitivity experiments, error attribution, domain-level comparisons, and qualitative OCR/RAG cases.

M1.justification: Semantic-noise construction changes from GPT-4o modifying structured text using OCR-error examples to eight image-distortion strategies followed by actual OCR using MinerU, GOT, and Qwen2.5-VL (Sec. 3.3; appendix). v2 also introduces entity-linked multi-page question construction and additional verification steps. These change the benchmark procedure, while the basic RAG pipeline remains.

E1.justification: v2 adds Administration to the six retained domains and expands coverage to Chinese-language, handwritten, historical, and distorted documents. Chart and reading-order evidence and explicitly multi-page questions extend the task requirements beyond v1's text, table, and formula questions (Secs. 3.1–3.2; appendix cases).

E2.justification: Table 2 replaces Qwen2-VL-72B and InternVL2-Llama3-76B with Qwen2.5-VL-72B and InternVL2.5-78B. Noise and table-format comparisons replace GPT-4o with Qwen2-72B, retaining the smaller generators and both retrievers. The separate generation comparison involving GPT-4o, Qwen2-VL-7B, and InternVL2-8B is removed.

E3.justification: The reported collection grows from 350 PDFs/4,598 Q&As to 1,261 PDFs/8,498 Q&As. Default retrieval depth changes from one to two chunks, and EM/top-5 reporting disappears. Noise calibration switches from edit distance to an affected-Q&A ratio; formatting-noise retrieval scoring excludes injected style commands, and semantic-noise results average three OCR systems (Secs. 4.1–4.3).

E4.justification: v2 revises the noise-sensitivity study, adds OCR-versus-RAG error attribution (Fig. 5), compares real and injected formatting-noise counts (Table S2), and adds annotated failure cases. Conversely, v1's VLM-input ablation, numerical simple-versus-detailed OCR-prompt comparison, and domain-specific noise curves are removed. The table-format analysis is retained with revised results.

E5.justification: v2 Table 1 adds ± values for question and answer lengths without identifying the dispersion statistic. Appendix II.5 newly specifies ten sampled GPT-4o answers per correctness check and repeated sampling audits; these concern dataset verification, not repeated benchmark trials. Neither version reports performance confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Results and rankings are substantially replaced. In v1 Table 2, Marker leads retrieval with 56.94 LCS@1 and MinerU leads overall with 36.84 F1@1; v2 reports Qwen2.5-VL-72B leading with 59.2 LCS and 31.1 overall F1. Changed data and retrieval settings prevent interpreting these as same-setting gains or losses. New evidence categories and error analyses add results. Nougat's v2 overall F1 remains internally inconsistent: 14.5 in Table 2 versus 22.2 in Table S5.

T1.justification: v2 Sec. 4.3 introduces the mathematical definition of r_noise as the fraction of Q&As whose evidence-to-perturbed-content LCS does not exceed 0.95. This is a limited new definition supporting noise calibration; neither version presents substantive theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The benchmark contribution broadens to challenging multilingual documents, additional evidence sources, and multi-page tasks. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion remove v1's explicit contribution concerning OCR-free VLM generation and the benefits of combining images with OCR text. The central claim that OCR noise undermines RAG remains.

C2.justification: v1 emphasizes pipeline OCR superiority and complementary image/OCR inputs. v2 instead attributes VLM OCR advantages to structured-data extraction and decoder resilience, while identifying paragraph merging as a distinct weakness. It adds interpretations of larger generators recovering from OCR errors and attributes weaker Markdown generation to unsupported merged cells (Secs. 4.2–4.3).

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands source-selection instructions, chart/image annotation rules, task-specific prompts, QA-verification thresholds, and image-distortion parameters. OCR software versions, hardware, and deterministic inference defaults remain documented. However, v1's direct project-code link disappears, replaced by a future benchmark-release statement; this changes access information without establishing actual resource availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for DUDE, OmniDocBench, GNHK, newer VLMs, DeepSeek-V3, spaCy, and LongDocURL, among others. It also emphasizes earlier benchmarks' insufficient coverage of challenging OCR documents. The existing related-work framework and central novelty positioning otherwise remain substantially intact.

P1.justification: Benchmark-construction and results-discussion paragraphs are substantially rewritten. The narrative removes the standalone VLM-generation section and adds error analysis. Appendix material is reorganized into separate benchmark-construction, noise-introduction, experimental-results, and case-study sections, with extensively revised prompt documentation.

P2.justification: The dataset overview is redesigned, Table 2 is reorganized around five evidence sources, and noise plots change axes and category groupings. Domain tables are restructured, while new error-attribution and case figures replace several older displays. Presentation defects remain: v2 Figs. S3 and S4 repeat the same example under different captions, and some other case captions misidentify their evidence type.

improvement.justification: Replacing v1's GPT-4o-written text corruption with image distortions processed by actual OCR systems substantially strengthens the central stress test's connection to OCR failures. v2 also improves question validation through oracle-answer consistency and single-context checks, while evidence-specific scores and error attribution clarify cascading failures. These gains outweigh the removed VLM-input/prompt ablations and code-access link, although inconsistent table totals and mislabeled appendix cases weaken reporting reliability.
